The *Chakkauddesa* ("Exposition of the Groups of Six") is the sixth section of the *mātikā* (schedule or table of contents) of the *Puggalapaññatti*, the fourth treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text lays out the matrix of human classifications or personality types grouped by sixes. SuttaCentral records one translation into a modern language [SuttaCentral]. No dedicated scholarly discussions or citations of this individual section were identified in the sampled research corpus.
According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits substantial internal Pali reuse, sharing 183 matching passages across 19 other Pali canonical and paracanonical works [DharmaNexus]. Its largest textual overlaps occur with the *Dasakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10; 73 matches), as well as the detailed elaboration found later in the same work, the *Chakkapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.6; 6 matches spanning §0.1–2.6 to §0.1–6.1_1) [DharmaNexus]. It also shows reuse connections with other chapters of the *Puggalapaññatti* (such as Pp 2.1 and Pp 2.9), the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, three sections of the *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 18, 21, and 22), and several commentarial and subcommentarial treatises including the *Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā*, *Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus records no cross-language matches with Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan texts meeting the score threshold [DharmaNexus].
